title: Suspected bacterial meningitis at 35, immunocompetent, on vancomycin and ceftriaxone without ampicillin

provenance.author: Claude Code (draft for owner review), case list approved by the owner

story: A previously healthy 35-year-old man presents with fever, headache and neck stiffness; CSF shows a neutrophilic pleocytosis with low glucose. He is not immunocompromised, pregnant, or a heavy alcohol user. Empiric vancomycin, ceftriaxone 2 g every 12 hours and dexamethasone are started; cultures are pending.

reference_answer: No intervention. Vancomycin plus a third-generation cephalosporin with dexamethasone is the empiric regimen for an immunocompetent adult under 50; ampicillin is not routinely needed. Narrow therapy when cultures return.
rationale: The negative pair of the Listeria case: the same presentation and regimen, but age and risk factors do not call for Listeria coverage. A rule that flags every meningitis regimen without ampicillin fails this case.
